title: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal Structure & Channels
source_organization: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs
text: The National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (https://cybercrime.gov.in/) is the official initiative of the Government of India, Ministry of Home Affairs, to facilitate victims and complainants to report cybercrime complaints online. The portal features dedicated reporting categories: 1. 'Report Crime Related to Women/Child', 2. 'Report Financial Fraud', and 3. 'Report Other Cyber Crimes' such as cyberstalking, hacking, identity theft, and online defamation. Complaints submitted through the portal are automatically routed to the state and district cyber police unit of the jurisdiction selected by the complainant for inquiry and legal action under the law.

title: Reporting Cybercrimes Against Women and Children
source_organization: Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), Government of India
text: Under the 'Report Crime Related to Women / Child' module on cybercrime.gov.in, victims have two distinct filing pathways: 1. 'Report Anonymously': Allows reporting non-consensual sexually explicit content, deepfakes, or child sexual abuse material without disclosing complainant identity or undergoing OTP verification. This option focuses on blocking abusive media, but police cannot provide incident investigation updates or follow up directly with the reporter. 2. 'Report and Track': Requires mobile OTP verification and complainant basic details, which generates a formal Complaint Acknowledgment Number (CAN) enabling tracking of police investigation and jurisdictional officer assignment.

title: National Cyber Financial Fraud Helpline 1930 & Golden Hour Reporting
source_organization: Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System (I4C)
text: The 1930 helpline (formerly 155260) connects complainants to the Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System operated by the Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C). In cases of financial extortion, sextortion involving monetary demands, or fraudulent UPI/bank transfers, victims should call 1930 immediately during the 'golden hour' (first 2-3 hours). The system coordinates directly with participating commercial banks, payment gateways, and wallet providers to freeze siphoned funds in transit before fraudsters withdraw them. Complainants should have transaction IDs, sender/receiver bank details, and timestamps ready.
review_notes: Verified via Ministry of Home Affairs national 1930 advisory

title: Section 66E Information Technology Act: Violation of Privacy
source_organization: Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice, Government of India
text: Section 66E of the Information Technology Act, 2000 penalizes the intentional capturing, publishing, or transmitting of images of a private area of any person without their consent, under circumstances violating the privacy of that person. The offense is punishable with imprisonment which may extend to three years or with a fine not exceeding two lakh rupees, or with both. In legal interpretation, 'private area' covers intimate areas, and transmission includes electronic sharing across messaging apps, social networks, or cloud drives.
review_notes: Statutory provision text verified via India Code (IT Act 2000 as amended)

title: Sections 67 & 67A IT Act: Electronic Publishing of Explicit Content
source_organization: Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice, Government of India
text: Sections 67 and 67A of the Information Technology Act, 2000 strictly penalize the electronic publication or transmission of obscene and sexually explicit acts respectively. Section 67 provides imprisonment up to three years on first conviction. Section 67A specifically addresses material containing sexually explicit acts or conduct, carrying imprisonment up to five years and fine up to ten lakh rupees on first conviction. Both sections apply to non-consensual distribution, blackmail with intimate media, and synthetic media / deepfake morphing depicting a person in sexually explicit postures.
review_notes: Statutory text verified via India Code

title: Stalking and Cyber Harassment Provisions under Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)
source_organization: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India
text: Under Section 78 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS, 2023), corresponding to Section 354D of the Indian Penal Code, any man who monitors the use by a woman of the internet, email, or any other form of electronic communication commits the offense of stalking. It is punishable with imprisonment up to three years for a first conviction and up to five years for a second conviction, along with a fine. Continuous unwanted direct messages, creation of duplicate accounts to bypass blocking, or tracking digital presence constitutes criminal cyberstalking.
review_notes: Verified against Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 enactments

title: Zero FIR Concept and Police Obligation to Register Complaints
source_organization: Ministry of Home Affairs Advisory / Supreme Court of India
text: A Zero FIR can be lodged at ANY police station in India, irrespective of where the alleged crime was committed or whether the station holds territorial jurisdiction. The police station is legally mandated to register the Zero FIR under serial number '0', conduct preliminary medical examination or basic inquiries if urgent, and promptly transfer the case documents to the police station possessing lawful territorial jurisdiction. Refusal by a police officer to register an FIR in cognizable offenses involving women is punishable under Section 199 of BNS (formerly Section 166A IPC).
review_notes: Verified via MHA Advisory on Zero FIR & Criminal Law Amendment

title: Digital Evidence Preservation Best Practices & Admissibility
source_organization: National Cyber Crime Training Centre / Ministry of Home Affairs
text: Preserving digital evidence safely is essential for legal proceedings under Section 63 of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023 (formerly Section 65B of the Indian Evidence Act). Key standards include: 1. Never crop, compress, filter, or annotate original screenshots; keep the full screen showing device time, battery status, and full sender handles. 2. Capture and record complete URLs (e.g., https://instagram.com/profile/...) rather than only display names. 3. Save raw email headers (.eml or full headers) to document origin IP routing. 4. Back up evidence to a secure offline flash drive or private cloud storage with Two-Factor Authentication. 5. Never engage in illegal hacking or endanger personal safety to collect evidence.
review_notes: Verified in accordance with BSA 2023 digital evidence guidelines

title: StopNCII.org Client-Side Hashing for Non-Consensual Image Removal
source_organization: South West Grid for Learning (SWGfL) / Revenge Porn Helpline
text: StopNCII.org is a free, privacy-protecting tool operated by the UK charity SWGfL to prevent the online sharing of non-consensual intimate images (NCII) on participating tech platforms (Meta/Facebook/Instagram, TikTok, Bumble, Reddit, OnlyFans, Threads). The tool operates client-side: unique cryptographic digital hashes are generated directly inside your web browser on your own device. The actual intimate photos or videos NEVER leave your device and are never uploaded to SWGfL or any server. Only the mathematical hashes are shared with participating platforms to automatically detect and block duplicate uploads.
review_notes: Verified via official StopNCII technical documentation at https://stopncii.org/

title: Take It Down Tool for Minors (Under 18 Content)
source_organization: National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC)
text: Take It Down is an anonymous service operated by the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children (NCMEC) to help remove or prevent the posting of sexually explicit images and videos taken of individuals when they were under 18 years old. Similar to StopNCII, Take It Down generates numerical hashes directly on the user device without uploading actual files. In India, creation, distribution, or possession of explicit media involving minors is severely penalised under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012 and Section 67B of the IT Act.
review_notes: Verified via NCMEC official service portal https://takeitdown.ncmec.org/

title: National Commission for Women (NCW) & Free Legal Aid via NALSA
source_organization: National Commission for Women & National Legal Services Authority (NALSA)
text: Under Section 12 of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, every woman in India is entitled to free legal services irrespective of her income or financial status. Free legal assistance is delivered through District Legal Services Authorities (DLSA), State Legal Services Authorities (SLSA), and Taluka Legal Services Committees. The National Commission for Women (NCW, 24x7 helpline: 7827170170) provides an escalation and grievance redressal forum for women whose complaints have not been registered by local police, facilitating legal counsel, inquiry escalation, and counselor intervention.
review_notes: Verified via NALSA portal and NCW helpline specifications

title: National Emergency Response Support System (ERSS 112) Overview
source_organization: Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), Government of India
text: ERSS 112 is India's unified 24x7 emergency response system integrating police, fire, health, and disaster management into a single toll-free number. In situations of active physical danger, assault, or being stalked in public, dialing 112 from any phone connects immediately to the nearest Emergency Response Centre (ERC). The service supports real-time Computer Aided Dispatch (CAD) to direct emergency response vehicles. If unable to speak, callers should keep the line active. In addition, Women Helpline 181 and Women Police Helpline 1091 provide dedicated crisis rescue.
